recommendations.rationale: Defer any controller-parameter change (including adopting tip-speed weighting or horizon/budget edits) because the only executed check is a single 0.01 s projected-model saved-state comparison for update 32, flagged advisory_only with ranking_changed false; it shows unused local braking authority at that state but cannot certify closed-loop settling or a dominant cause.

Defer further progress on separating objective weighting from solver early-stop plan quality until the non-retained historical full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces (or a wider read of retained middle-run updates) are available, since this probe and the retained inventory cannot distinguish those mechanisms.

attribution.reason: At the one probed saved state, the braking-box arm's projected endpoint tip speed (0.6432770054642075 m/s) is below the recorded arm's sampled speeds at matched offsets (1.363441334968781 / 1.4178902060841199 / 1.4500559687241532 m/s) over the same 0.01 s step, so under the projected model the recorded applied tension for update 32 did leave locally available braking authority unused. Scope is one saved state, one 0.01 s interval, projected model, advisory-only result; it does not explain or rank the closed-loop settling failure.

Recorded parameters set holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 with a 0.02 m/s tip-speed scale and small velocity/terminal-velocity weights, consistent with a position-dominated objective that attains reach (0.007642608585867386 m) while leaving tip speed high (terminal 0.6351726092425104 m/s). Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance, and this probe cannot separate weighting from solver early-stop plan quality.

Sampled updates stopped with User_Requested_Stop (0, 32, 33) against a single Solve_Succeeded, solves of about 15 s against the 15 s feasible-return budget, mean update 17.075238151415917 s, and sampled effective horizons falling to 3 and 1 intervals at updates 32 and 34 versus a configured 10; such short effective horizons plausibly leave little lookahead in which to null tip velocity. No warm plans or iteration traces are retained to check plan quality.

The braking-box arm asks for more than the 8.0 N per-tendon limit on two tendons (near_t2, far_t0 at 8.0 N), so braking demand at this state exceeds the force limits; but within those limits the modelled braking box still cut endpoint speed to 0.6432770054642075 m/s while the recorded input (max 6.991578354461397 N, below limits) let speed rise. Limit proximity therefore does not by itself explain the high tip speed at this state, though it may bind where sampled requested tensions approached 7.99 N.

Sampled matched-endpoint tip differences are small (<=1.2 mm) but are explicitly scoped as projected-prediction versus backend endpoint, not full-state agreement; the check evaluates both arms with the projected model, so it cannot test this mechanism, and a 0.01 s probe cannot explain an entire settling failure.

The stated hypothesis that braking authority at this state is so bounded that the braking-box input yields an endpoint speed close to the recorded input's is contradicted here: the braking-box arm ends at 0.6432770054642075 m/s against recorded-arm speeds >=1.36 m/s over the same step, so local authority was sufficient for a large modelled speed reduction (its two saturated channels do bound the achievable reduction). This ruling applies to one state and the projected model only.

The recorded arm leaves braking authority unused, and both objective weighting (recorded 0.0 holding tip-speed weight) and early-stop plan quality predict that same local endpoint difference, so this probe cannot distinguish them; each remains individually possible.

Under this run's synchronous contract the controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time; the 17.075238151415917 s mean update time and near-15 s solves are compute overruns and evidence of solver load, not simulated-time stalls.

facts.statement: The run passed terminal reach (reach_passed true; terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance) but failed sampled settling: late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810152739742807 and late_max_error_m 0.05813810428573256 both exceed the settling criteria (position limit 0.01 m, speed limit 0.02 m/s, window 0.05 s), and terminal_speed_m_s 0.6351726092425104 remains above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

Sampled controller updates record optimization_raw_status 'User_Requested_Stop' at updates 0, 32 and 33 and 'Solve_Succeeded' at update 34, while the run summary records only 1 Solve_Succeeded; sampled optimization_solve_s values are 15.077540499856696 s (update 32), 15.06219010008499 s (update 33) and 2.885958099970594 s (update 34) with mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 against a 0.01 s control period, and sampled effective horizons are 10 (updates 1, 2), 5 (update 30), 3 (update 32) and 1 (update 34) control intervals against a configured horizon of 10.

In the completed prediction_braking check at update 32's saved projected state (horizon 0.01 s, integration step 0.002 s, implicit Euler, model.gvs@1.0.0), the recorded-input arm's projected tip speed rises across the step (1.363441334968781 m/s at t=0.002 s, 1.4178902060841199 m/s at t=0.006 s, 1.4500559687241532 m/s at t=0.008 s) and its endpoint velocity at t=0.01 s is [0.5974534504742045, -0.7026564897169398, -1.1628511059575015] m/s, whereas the instantaneous braking-box arm (tension [0.0, 0.0, 8.0, 8.0, 0.0, 0.0] N) reaches projected endpoint speed 0.6432770054642075 m/s at t=0.01 s (0.5456310113130424 m/s at t=0.008 s); no handle in this context records the recorded arm's endpoint speed, and the two-arm difference is not a retrieved computation.

The check result is flagged advisory_only true with ranking_changed false and search 'analytic bounded linear objective on unilateral tension box; no iterative input optimizer'; it was evaluated from saved projected state /32/measured_initial_state with both arms under the projected model, the two-arm computation cost 8.567264799959958 s, and the braking-box tension vector places near_t2 and far_t0 at 8.0 N, the per-tendon force limit listed in the retained force-limit inventory entry.

Recorded controller parameters include holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02, velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001, tension_weight 0.0001, variation_weight 0.001, holding_brake_lead_s 0.0, configured horizon 10 intervals, seed_position_tolerance_fraction 0.5, max_iterations 120 and feasible-return budget_s 15.0; initialization_selected is 29, noninitialization_selected 6, and full_snapshots_available is false.

The probed update 32 interval (start 0.32 s, prediction endpoint 0.33 s, world frame) carries reconstructed measured tip speed 1.5810152739742807 m/s, obtained by deterministic reconstruction J_site(q_backend) @ qdot_backend from the sealed robot model and recorded joint order (not a direct velocity measurement), with predicted next error 0.016277969122167637 m.

Sampled matched-interval comparisons show small projected-versus-backend endpoint tip differences (0.0004104875470393126 m at update 0, 0.0009375940357077928 m at update 2, 0.001183439178222365 m at update 34); the recorded scope note states these compare projected GVS predictions against full serial-backend endpoints and are classified as recorded projected states, not full backend-state error.

limitations: Model limit: both check arms were evaluated with projected model model.gvs@1.0.0 from the single saved projected state /32/measured_initial_state, and the result is advisory_only, so the projected-GVS versus full serial-backend model mismatch could not be tested.

Horizon/integration limit: the probe covers one 0.01 s interval integrated with implicit Euler at 0.002 s steps; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot explain an entire closed-loop settling failure, and instantaneous deceleration need not persist during a held-input rollout.

Input limit: the arms are the recorded applied tensions for update 32 and an analytically computed bounded braking-box input on a unilateral tension box with no iterative input optimizer; the braking-box arm is a model-possibility bound, not a controller-feasible plan, and the arms differ in construction as well as in outcome.

State coverage: only one saved state (update 32, t = 0.32 s) was probed; sampled backend motion and projected state vectors for the middle of the run (about 0.01-0.29 s) were not displayed in this context.

Non-retention: historical full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces (control_snapshots.json) are not retained, so objective weighting and solver early-stop plan quality cannot be separated directly.
Capability limit: no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability is available, so no mechanism here is certified as the dominant settling cause.

Even the best modelled one-step braking at this state ends at 0.6432770054642075 m/s, above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit, so unused local braking authority is not by itself a satisfying closed-loop explanation.

Interpretation limits: the 17.075238151415917 s mean update time and deadline misses are compute overruns, not simulated-time feedback delay, and raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance (no cost-contribution decomposition is available).
recommended_actions: Advisory only: do not adopt a controller-parameter change on the strength of this single saved-state probe, which is measured under the projected model over one 0.01 s step and does not certify closed-loop settling.

If the weighting-versus-plan-quality question must be settled, obtain the non-retained historical full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces, or read a wider sample of retained middle-run updates, before any control change.

If the unused local braking authority is to be acted on, test the braking-box gap at additional saved states (including states where sampled requested tensions approached the 8.0 N per-tendon limit) before considering any control change.
